exampleAnswers.title: Simplifying Expression Using an Alternate Form of the Pythagorean Identity

question.explanation:
First, we expand the parentheses and simplify:

\begin{align} (\sin \theta -1)( \sin \theta +1) &= \sin^2 \theta + \sin \theta - \sin \theta - 1 \\[3pt] &= \sin^2 \theta -1\\[3pt] &= -(1- \sin^2 \theta) \end{align}

Now, we can use the identity $1 - \sin^2 \theta = \cos^2 \theta$ to rewrite the expression on the right-hand side. \[ -(1- \sin^2 \theta)= -\cos^2 \theta \]

Therefore, we conclude that: \[ (\sin \theta -1)( \sin \theta +1) = - \cos^2 \theta \]

example.title: Simplifying Expression Using an Alternate Form of the Pythagorean Identity

question.explanation:
First, we expand the parentheses: \begin{align} \sec{x}\left( \cos x - \cos^3 {x} \right) = \sec{x} \cdot \cos{x} - \sec{x} \cdot \cos^3{x} \end{align}

Then, we use the identity $\sec{x} = \dfrac{1}{\cos{x}}$ to further simplify the expression: \begin{align} \sec{x} \cdot \cos{x} - \sec{x} \cdot \cos^3{x} & = \dfrac{1}{\cos{x}} \cdot \cos{x} - \dfrac{1}{\cos{x}} \cdot \cos^3{x}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\cos{x}}{\cos{x}} - \dfrac{\cos^3{x}}{\cos{x}}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\cos{x}}{\cos{x}} - \dfrac{\cos^2{x} \cdot \cos{x}}{\cos{x}}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\cancel{\cos{x}}}{\cancel{\cos{x}}} - \dfrac{\cos^2{x} \cdot \cancel{\cos{x}}}{\cancel{\cos{x}}}\\[5pt] & = 1 - \cos^2{x} \end{align}

Now, we can use the identity $\sin^2{x} = 1 - \cos^2{x}$ to rewrite the expression on the right-hand side.

Therefore, we conclude that:

\[ \sec{x}\left( \cos x - \cos^3 {x} \right) = \sin^2{x} \]

example.title: Simplifying Expression Using an Alternate Form of the Pythagorean Identity

question.explanation:
First, we expand the parentheses: \begin{align} 2\sin x \left(\csc{x} - \csc{x} \cdot \cos^2{x} \right) = 2\sin{x} \cdot \csc{x} - 2\sin{x} \cdot \csc{x} \cdot \cos^2{x} \end{align}

Then, we use the identity $\csc{x} = \dfrac{1}{\sin{x}}$ to further simplify the expression: \begin{align*} \require{cancel} 2\sin{x} \cdot \csc{x} - 2\sin{x} \cdot \csc{x} \cdot \cos^2{x} & = 2\sin{x} \cdot \dfrac{1}{\sin{x}} - 2\sin{x} \cdot \dfrac{1}{\sin{x}} \cdot \cos^2{x}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{2\sin{x}}{\sin{x}} - \dfrac{2\sin{x} \cdot \cos^2{x}}{\sin{x}}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{2\cancel{\sin{x}}}{\cancel{\sin{x}}} - \dfrac{2\cancel{\sin{x}} \cdot \cos^2{x}}{\cancel{\sin{x}}}\\[5pt] & = 2 - 2\cos^2{x}\\[5pt] & = 2(1 - \cos^2{x}) \end{align*}

Now, we can use the identity $\sin^2 x = 1 - \cos^2 x$ to rewrite the expression on the right-hand side.

Therefore, we conclude that: \[ 2\sin x \left(\csc{x} - \csc{x} \cdot \cos^2{x} \right) = 2\sin^2 x \]

exampleAnswers.title: Simplifying Rational Expressions Using an Alternate Form of the Pythagorean Identity

question.explanation:
First, we factor the expression: \begin{align} \dfrac{1}{\sin \theta} - \dfrac{ \cos^2\theta}{\sin \theta} &= \dfrac{1}{\sin \theta} - \dfrac{1}{\sin \theta} \cdot \cos^2\theta\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{\sin \theta} (1 - \cos ^2\theta) \end{align}

Then, we use $\sin^2{\theta} = 1 - \cos ^2\theta $ to simplify the expression in the parentheses: \begin{align} \require{cancel} \dfrac{1}{\sin \theta} (1 - \cos ^2\theta) & = \dfrac{1}{\sin \theta} \cdot \sin^2\theta \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{ \sin^2\theta}{\sin \theta} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\cancel{\sin\theta} \sin\theta}{\cancel{\sin\theta}} \\[5pt] &= \sin\theta \end{align}

Hence, we conclude that: \[ \dfrac{1}{\sin \theta} - \dfrac{ \cos^2\theta}{\sin \theta} =\sin\theta \]

example.title: Simplifying Rational Expressions Using an Alternate Form of the Pythagorean Identity

question.explanation:
First, we rewrite the denominator using $1-\sin^2 \theta = \cos^2 \theta\mathbin{:}$ \[ \dfrac{\sin^2\theta\cot^2\theta}{1-\sin^2\theta} = \dfrac{\sin^2\theta\cot^2\theta}{\cos^2\theta} \]

Next, we simplify by separating out the factors, and use the identity $\cot\theta = \dfrac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta},$ as follows:

\begin{align*} \require{cancel} \dfrac{\sin^2\theta\cot^2\theta}{\cos^2\theta} &= \dfrac{\sin^2\theta}{\cos^2\theta}\cdot \cot^2\theta\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\sin^2\theta}{\cos^2\theta}\cdot \dfrac{\cos^2\theta}{\sin^2\theta}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\cancel{\sin^2\theta}}{\cos^2\theta}\cdot \dfrac{\cos^2\theta}{\cancel{\sin^2\theta}}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{\cos^2\theta}\cdot \dfrac{\cos^2\theta}{1}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{\cancel{\cos^2\theta}}\cdot \dfrac{\cancel{\cos^2\theta}}{1}\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{1}{1}\cdot\dfrac{1}{1}\\[5pt] &=1 \end{align*}

Therefore, we conclude that:

\[ \dfrac{\sin^2\theta\cot^2\theta}{1-\sin^2\theta} = 1 \]

exampleAnswers.title: Simplifying Expressions by Factoring an Alternate Form of the Pythagorean Identity

question.explanation:
First, we rewrite the numerator using $1-\cos^2 x = \sin^2 x.$

\[ \dfrac{\sin^2 x}{\cos x-1} = \dfrac{1-\cos^2 x}{\cos x-1} \]

Next, we factor the numerator as a difference of squares, and simplify:

\begin{align*} \require{cancel} \dfrac{1-\cos^2 x}{\cos x-1} &= \dfrac{(1+\cos x)(1-\cos x)}{\cos x-1} \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{(1+\cos x)(1-\cos x)}{1-\cos x} \\[5pt] &=-\dfrac{(1+\cos x)\cancel{(1-\cos x)}}{\cancel{1-\cos x }} \\[5pt] &=-\dfrac{1+ \cos x}{1} \\[5pt] &=-(1+\cos {x}) \end{align*}

Therefore, we conclude that:

\[ \dfrac{\sin^2 x}{1-\cos x} =-(1+\cos {x}) \]

example.title: Simplifying Expressions by Factoring an Alternate Form of the Pythagorean Identity

question.explanation:
First, we rewrite the numerator of the second term using $1-\sin^2 x = \cos^2 x.$

\[ 1- \dfrac{\cos^2 x}{\sin x +1} = 1- \dfrac{1-\sin^2 x}{\sin x +1} \]

Next, we factor the numerator of the second term as a difference of squares, and simplify:

\begin{align*} \require{cancel} 1- \dfrac{1-\sin^2 x}{\sin x +1} &= 1- \dfrac{(1+\sin x)(1-\sin x)}{\sin x +1} \\[5pt] &= 1- \dfrac{\cancel{(1+\sin x)}(1-\sin x)}{\cancel{\sin x +1}} \\[5pt] &= 1- \dfrac{1-\sin x}{1} \\[5pt] &= 1- (1-\sin {x}) \\[5pt] &= \sin {x} \end{align*}
